_note: What the face contract still fixes, now that expressions are data. Gazes and panel modes ARE still fixed here: they are drawn by branches compiled into both renderers, so adding one is a code change in two languages, and this file plus test/face-spec.test.mjs is what stops those branches drifting apart. Expressions are no longer fixed — they are JSON files on each device (spc-agent/expressions/*.json, plus /etc/spc/expressions and ~/.spc/expressions), loaded by spc_expressions.py and served from the device's GET /expressions. mcp-tools.js therefore validates gaze and panel mode against this file and does NOT validate expression at all; the device does that, because only the device knows what a user dropped on it.
_builtin_note: builtin_expressions is the ten that ship, duplicated in spc_expressions.py's BUILTIN dict so a device that lost its expressions directory mid-deploy still boots its screen. It is NOT an enum — it is the floor every device is guaranteed to clear, and mcp-tools.js quotes it in spc_expression's description so a model has something safe to reach for without a lookup. A device may have more; spc_list_devices reports each one's actual list.
_geometry_note: Shape names are the browser page's (spc_face.py), and an expression JSON's inline coordinates are in its 400x300 face box, because that is the space a user can look at while drawing one. spc_fb.py maps both onto framebuffer units — it calls a closed eye "arc_down" internally and scales canonical coordinates by a measured constant. The two builtin shape tables stay separate on purpose: they were hand-tuned, not derived from each other, and forcing them through one set of numbers would move faces that are already right.
